title: Local name of the Nazca region meaning a laboratory for hybridization

tellings.quote: Uh the the the local region translates to laboratory for insemination and hybridization.
And there is a little book published in 2004 by a local author from Nazca that talked about various sites in the Nazca area.
tellings.difference: Credits a 2004 book by a local Nazca author and adds 'cloning' to the meaning; the story is dated 2006.
tellings.link_reason: Both claim a local name for a Nazca site or region translates as a laboratory for hybridization; this telling gives the 2004 local book as the source.

as_told.title: 2004 Nazca book: site name means cloning and hybridization laboratory

plain: The old local name of the Nazca region in Peru is said to translate as "laboratory for insemination and hybridization". Michels raises it in a 2025 episode with the guests Jay Anderson and Kurt Metzger, crediting a book from 2006 that he does not name. If true, it would suggest that the people who once lived there linked the place to the making of mixed or hybrid beings. The researcher and explorer Thierry Jamin, who studies the three-fingered mummies found in Peru, tells it in another 2025 episode with a different source and date. He credits "a little book published in 2004 by a local author from Nazca" that described various sites around Nazca. In Jamin's telling the name also takes in cloning. So the two tellers agree on the meaning but not on the book's date: Michels says 2006 and Jamin says 2004.
